source: Star Schema Benchmark, P. O'Neil, E. O'Neil, X. Chen, Revision 3, June 5, 2009: Section 2.1 (PARTSUPP dropped), 2.2 (LINEORDER), 2.3 (PART), 2.4 (SUPPLIER), 2.5 (CUSTOMER), 2.6 (DATE), Appendix A (the TPC-H tables it is derived from). The instance is derived from TPC-H dbgen output by these rules (gen_ssb.py, CHOICES), not generated by ssb-dbgen.
rule: Sigma* of a table consists of its primary key, the documented hierarchies and every FD that a rule of the specification forces on every instance ("sure": true). Where the specification leaves a column open, gen_ssb.py makes a stated choice, and an FD that holds only because of that choice, or only because the data is derived from TPC-H, is listed with "sure": false. Such an FD holds on every instance of this construction. Columns that are random in the construction determine nothing, even when unique on the instance.

truth.justification: Primary Key: C_CUSTKEY.
C_NAME is 'Customer' followed by C_CUSTKEY, an injective function of the key (the construction keeps the TPC-H form 'Customer#' with 9 digits).
C_CITY is the first 9 characters of C_NATION, blank-extended, followed by a digit 0-9, and the 9-character prefixes of the 25 TPC-H nation names are distinct (UNITED KI and UNITED ST differ).

C_NATION and C_REGION take the 25 nation names and 5 region names of TPC-H, where each nation lies in one region (N_REGIONKEY references R_REGIONKEY). Query flight Q3 groups customer nations within a region.
The construction copies C_PHONE from TPC-H, whose country code is the nation key + 10. SSB 2.5 gives only the format '43-617-354-1222', so the SSB specification does not force this FD.

ssb_customer.random_columns: C_ADDRESS and C_MKTSEGMENT are random (copied from TPC-H). The digit of C_CITY is random.
ssb_customer.gold_design_note: SSB publishes the denormalized dimension (one table). The gold design is its snowflake along the documented hierarchy city -> nation -> region. It does not preserve the unsure C_PHONE -> C_NATION.

truth.justification: Primary Key: S_SUPPKEY.
S_NAME is 'Supplier' followed by S_SUPPKEY, an injective function of the key (the construction keeps the TPC-H form 'Supplier#' with 9 digits).
S_CITY is the first 9 characters of S_NATION, blank-extended, followed by a digit 0-9, and the 9-character prefixes of the 25 TPC-H nation names are distinct.
S_NATION and S_REGION take the 25 nation names and 5 region names of TPC-H, where each nation lies in one region. Query flights Q2 to Q4 restrict suppliers by region and group them by nation.
The construction copies S_PHONE from TPC-H, whose country code is the nation key + 10. SSB 2.4 gives only the format, so the SSB specification does not force this FD.

ssb_supplier.random_columns: S_ADDRESS is random (copied from TPC-H). The digit of S_CITY is random.
ssb_supplier.gold_design_note: Snowflake of the published dimension along city -> nation -> region. It does not preserve the unsure S_PHONE -> S_NATION.

truth.justification: Primary Key: P_PARTKEY.
P_BRAND1 is P_CATEGORY followed by a number 1-40, 'a division of P_CATEGORY'. P_CATEGORY has fixed length 7, so it is the prefix of P_BRAND1.
P_CATEGORY is 'MFGR#' followed by two digits 1-5, 'a division of P_MFGR', and P_MFGR is 'MFGR#' followed by the first of them.

ssb_part.random_columns: P_NAME (two random colour words, not unique), P_COLOR, P_TYPE, P_SIZE and P_CONTAINER are random. The specification leaves the relation between P_COLOR and P_NAME open; the construction draws P_COLOR independently, so no FD links them.
ssb_part.gold_design_note: Snowflake of the published dimension along brand1 -> category -> mfgr.

truth.justification: Primary Key: D_DATEKEY. Every column describes the day.
D_DATE ('December 22, 1998') and D_DATEKEY (YYYYMMDD) both name the day.
D_DAYOFWEEK (Sunday..Saturday) and D_DAYNUMINWEEK (1-7) are the name and the number of the weekday.
The number of the weekday gives its name, whether it ends the week and whether it is a weekday rather than a weekend day, whichever day the week starts on.
D_MONTH (January..December) and D_MONTHNUMINYEAR (1-12) are the name and the number of the month.
As above.
D_YEARMONTHNUM is YYYYMM, which gives the year, the month and D_YEARMONTH ('Mar1998').
D_YEARMONTH ('Mar1998') names the same month as YYYYMM.
YYYYMM is composed of the year and the month number.
A year and a day number in it identify the day.
A month and a day number in it identify the day.

A day number in the year falls in the same month in every year, except that from day 60 on a leap year is one day behind. The day number in the month then differs, so the two day numbers together determine the month.
A day number falls in different months only where the common year starts a month and the leap year, one day behind, ends the previous month, and the last-day-in-month flag tells these two apart.
With the construction's weeks, week w covers day numbers 7w-12 to 7w of every year, while equal day numbers of the month in different months lie at least 27 day numbers apart.

A selling season of the construction spans at most three consecutive months and never contains both February and March, so its days with equal day numbers of the month lie 30, 31 or 61 days apart, never a multiple of 7, and the weekday tells them apart.
The days of the previous FD differ in weekday by 2, 3 or 5 modulo 7, so at most one of them falls on a weekend, and the weekday flag then decides whether the day is the Saturday.

Holds because the construction numbers weeks within the year, each week containing every weekday at most once. It fails for ISO weeks, where the first days of January can belong to the last week of the previous year.
Weeks start on Sunday and week 1 is the week of January 1, so the day number and the weekday give the weekday of January 1 and hence the week number.
The construction assigns the selling season by month.
The construction marks only fixed-date holidays (January 1, July 4, December 25). Floating holidays such as Thanksgiving would break this FD.

ssb_date.random_columns: None: the date table is a function of the calendar. Sigma* is meant to hold on every range of years, so an FD that holds only on 1992-1998 is accidental; build.py checks Sigma* against the minimal FDs of the same construction over 1601-2000, a full 400-year Gregorian cycle (calendar_check).
ssb_date.gold_design_note: SSB publishes the dimension as one table and documents no snowflake for it; truth_design gives the 3NF designs of Sigma*.

truth.justification: Compound Primary Key: LO_ORDERKEY, LO_LINENUMBER.
LINEORDER combines LINEITEM and ORDERS. Customer, order date and priority are columns of the order, and LO_ORDTOTALPRICE brings over O_TOTALPRICE, marked (ORDER).
LO_REVENUE = (lo_extendedprice*(100-lo_discount))/100.
For a fixed extended price of at least 100 units, the revenue strictly decreases with the discount. The TPC-H prices are at least 901.00, but the SSB specification states no lower bound.

The construction inherits L_EXTENDEDPRICE = L_QUANTITY * P_RETAILPRICE with a fixed price per part. SSB 2.3 note (d) drops P_RETAILPRICE because part prices change over time and recovers the price of an order as LO_EXTENDEDPRICE/LO_QUANTITY, so under the SSB semantics a part may have different prices in different orders.
As above, with a positive price per part.
With the price P >= 901.00 of the part fixed, LO_REVENUE = floor(LO_QUANTITY * P * (100 - LO_DISCOUNT) / 100) strictly increases with the quantity.

The construction takes LO_SUPPLYCOST from the frozen TPC-H PARTSUPP, as Section 2.1 describes. Section 2.1 also argues that supply costs change over time, which is why the cost moves into the fact table, so the SSB semantics does not force this FD.

ssb_lineorder.random_columns: LO_LINENUMBER, LO_PARTKEY, LO_QUANTITY, LO_DISCOUNT, LO_TAX and LO_SHIPMODE are random per line, LO_CUSTKEY, LO_ORDERDATE and LO_ORDERPRIORITY per order. LO_SUPPKEY is one of the suppliers of the part, chosen at random. LO_COMMITDATE adds a random offset to the order date.
ssb_lineorder.gold_design_note: SSB publishes LINEORDER as one denormalized fact table. The gold design splits it back into its TPC-H origin, lines and orders. The line schema is not in 3NF under Sigma* (revenue and the unsure price and cost FDs).
